flashcards.front: Pooled vs. personal host pools
flashcards.back: Pooled host pools let many users share multi-session session hosts, load-balanced by the pool. Personal host pools assign one user to one dedicated session host, either automatically or by direct assignment, much like a traditional VDI desktop.
flashcards.detail: A personal host pool is the right fit when a user needs persistent local state or admin rights on their own VM; a pooled host pool with FSLogix is the standard choice for stateless, cost-efficient shared desktops.

flashcards.front: Breadth-first vs. depth-first load balancing
flashcards.back: Breadth-first spreads new sessions evenly across all available session hosts in a pooled host pool. Depth-first fills one session host up to its configured maximum session limit before sending new sessions to the next host.
flashcards.detail: Depth-first pairs naturally with autoscale, since it concentrates load onto fewer hosts and leaves other hosts empty and safe to deallocate; breadth-first favors performance by spreading load thin across more hosts.

flashcards.front: Automatic vs. direct assignment in a personal host pool
flashcards.back: Automatic assignment lets Azure Virtual Desktop assign the first available session host to a user the first time they connect. Direct assignment has an admin manually assign a specific session host to a specific user ahead of time.
flashcards.detail: Once a user is assigned, they always land on that same session host on every future connection, regardless of which assignment method put them there.

flashcards.front: Windows 11/10 Enterprise multi-session
flashcards.back: A special SKU of Windows Enterprise, licensed for Azure Virtual Desktop, that lets multiple users run concurrent, isolated desktop sessions on a single virtual machine, something ordinary Windows client licensing does not permit.
flashcards.detail: Multi-session is what makes pooled host pools cost-efficient; it is available only through Azure Virtual Desktop, not as a general Azure Marketplace Windows client image outside AVD.

flashcards.front: Azure Compute Gallery for AVD images
flashcards.back: A repository for storing, versioning, and sharing custom session host images across subscriptions and regions, replacing ad hoc managed image copies with replicated, versioned image definitions.
flashcards.detail: Compute Gallery lets you stage a new image version, test it in a validation host pool, then roll it out, giving controlled, repeatable image lifecycle management instead of hand-built golden images.

flashcards.front: Workspaces, application groups, and host pools
flashcards.back: A host pool is a collection of session hosts. An application group publishes either RemoteApp programs or a full Desktop from a host pool to users. A workspace is a logical container that groups application groups together for publishing to end users.
flashcards.detail: Users subscribe to a workspace, which surfaces every application group (and therefore every host pool) assigned to them, in one feed.

flashcards.front: Mixing RemoteApp and Desktop app groups on one host pool
flashcards.back: A pooled host pool can host multiple RemoteApp application groups, but Microsoft recommends not assigning the same users both a RemoteApp app group and a Desktop app group from the same host pool, since it causes duplicate icons and can be confusing for users.
flashcards.detail: A personal host pool, by contrast, only supports a single Desktop application group, not RemoteApp groups.

flashcards.front: FSLogix Profile Containers
flashcards.back: FSLogix stores a user's entire Windows profile inside a VHD/VHDX file on network storage, attached to the OS at sign-in, so the profile looks and behaves like a native local profile even though the user may land on a different session host every time.
flashcards.detail: This is what makes a pooled, stateless multi-session host pool practical; without it, a user reconnecting to a different session host would see a brand-new, empty profile.

flashcards.front: FSLogix Cloud Cache
flashcards.back: An FSLogix feature that writes profile changes to a local cache first and asynchronously replicates them to one or more configured storage locations (providers), giving redundancy and resilience if one storage location becomes unavailable.
flashcards.detail: Cloud Cache can replicate across multiple storage providers in different regions, which standard Profile Containers pointed at a single file share cannot do on their own.

flashcards.front: MSIX app attach
flashcards.back: Delivers applications packaged as MSIX from a network share, attaching them to a session host at user sign-in as a virtual disk, without installing the application into the OS image. The app appears in the Start menu but its files never touch the local disk.
flashcards.detail: Because nothing is installed into the golden image, app updates just mean adding a new MSIX package version; session hosts and the master image stay untouched.

flashcards.front: Azure Files vs. Azure NetApp Files for FSLogix
flashcards.back: Azure Files (Premium tier recommended) is the common, simpler choice for FSLogix profile storage at small-to-medium scale. Azure NetApp Files offers lower latency and higher IOPS/throughput, and is the recommended choice for large-scale or performance-sensitive deployments.
flashcards.detail: Azure NetApp Files requires its own delegated subnet and capacity pool, which adds setup complexity that a straightforward Azure Files Premium share does not.

flashcards.front: RDP Shortpath
flashcards.back: Establishes a direct UDP-based transport between the Remote Desktop client and the session host, bypassing the usual TCP relay through the Remote Desktop Gateway, to reduce latency and improve responsiveness.
flashcards.detail: RDP Shortpath for managed networks needs direct line-of-sight connectivity, such as a VPN or ExpressRoute, while RDP Shortpath for public networks uses STUN/TURN-based NAT traversal for clients anywhere on the internet.

flashcards.front: Planning for network bandwidth and latency
flashcards.back: Round-trip time (RTT) between the client and the Azure region hosting the session host is the dominant factor in perceived responsiveness; Microsoft's Azure Virtual Desktop Experience Estimator tool helps assess expected experience for a given network path.
flashcards.detail: As a rule of thumb, an RTT under roughly 150 ms gives a good interactive experience, while higher RTT increasingly degrades responsiveness regardless of raw bandwidth.

flashcards.front: Validation host pools
flashcards.back: A host pool flagged with the 'Validation environment' setting receives Azure Virtual Desktop service updates before general availability, letting an organization test agent and service changes on a small, low-risk pool before they reach production host pools.
flashcards.detail: This is purely a service/agent-update rollout ring; it has nothing to do with testing your own custom session host images, which is instead handled through Azure Compute Gallery image versions.

flashcards.front: VHD vs. VHDX for FSLogix containers
flashcards.back: FSLogix can store profile and Office containers as either VHD or VHDX files. VHDX is the recommended default: it is more resilient to power failures and supports larger container sizes than the older VHD format.
flashcards.detail: The container format is a per-configuration setting (VHDLocations plus a VHD/VHDX flag), not something the end user ever sees or manages.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Entra-joined vs. hybrid Entra-joined vs. AD DS-joined session hosts
flashcards.back: A Microsoft Entra-joined session host trusts only Entra ID, with no on-premises Active Directory involved. A hybrid Entra-joined host is joined to an on-premises AD DS domain that is synced to Entra ID. An AD DS-joined host is joined only to on-premises AD DS.
flashcards.detail: Microsoft Entra-joined session hosts are the simplest to deploy since they need no domain controllers or line-of-sight to on-premises AD, but historically needed extra configuration (like Entra Kerberos) for FSLogix profiles on Azure Files.

flashcards.front: Conditional Access for Azure Virtual Desktop
flashcards.back: Conditional Access policies can target the Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows Cloud Login Microsoft Entra enterprise apps, requiring controls such as multi-factor authentication or a compliant device before a user can establish a remote session.
flashcards.detail: Both apps typically need to be included in a Conditional Access policy together so that the requirement is enforced consistently across the web client, the native Remote Desktop client, and the RDP protocol's own authentication handshake.

flashcards.front: Built-in Azure Virtual Desktop RBAC roles
flashcards.back: Desktop Virtualization User lets a user access assigned application groups. Desktop Virtualization Contributor grants full management of Azure Virtual Desktop objects like host pools and app groups, but not the underlying VMs. Desktop Virtualization Virtual Machine Contributor manages the session host VMs themselves. Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator manages session hosts, including enabling/disabling new connections and sending messages.
flashcards.detail: Desktop Virtualization Contributor alone cannot restart or resize a session host VM; that needs the separate Virtual Machine Contributor role (or the general Azure Virtual Machine Contributor role) as well.

flashcards.front: Session host security baselines
flashcards.back: Microsoft publishes a security baseline for Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts (built on the general Windows security baseline) covering settings like restricting drive/clipboard/printer redirection, disabling unneeded services, and hardening the RDP listener.
flashcards.detail: Applying the baseline through Group Policy or Microsoft Intune settings catalog policies is the recommended, supported way to harden session hosts consistently at scale, rather than manually tweaking each image.

flashcards.front: Screen capture protection
flashcards.back: An RDP property that blocks a remote session's content from being captured by screenshot tools or screen-sharing/recording applications on the client, protecting sensitive on-screen data such as clinical or financial records.
flashcards.detail: It works by blacking out the session content whenever a capture attempt is detected, which also means any application relying on capturing the remote screen (like some remote-assistance tools) is blocked from doing so.

flashcards.front: Session watermarking
flashcards.back: An RDP property that overlays a visible, tiled watermark across the session containing information such as the connecting user's UPN, session host name, and IP address, deterring users from photographing or screen-capturing sensitive session content.
flashcards.detail: Watermarking is a deterrent control, not a technical block; it works together with, not instead of, screen capture protection when strong data-exfiltration controls are required.

flashcards.front: Least-privilege access on session hosts
flashcards.back: End users should not be members of the local Administrators group on session hosts; day-to-day AVD access should flow through the Desktop Virtualization User role and app group assignment, keeping local admin rights reserved for a small set of trusted administrators.
flashcards.detail: Because a pooled session host is shared by many users, giving any one user local admin rights risks that user affecting every other user sharing the same host.

flashcards.front: Configuring FSLogix (ADMX templates and registry)
flashcards.back: FSLogix ships ADMX/ADML template files that add a 'FSLogix Profile Containers' node to Group Policy, letting admins configure settings like the VHD storage location(s), container size, and enabled state through GPO instead of editing the registry on every image.
flashcards.detail: The same settings can equally be pushed as registry values through Microsoft Intune configuration profiles for session hosts that are not domain-joined to an on-premises AD.

flashcards.front: FSLogix Office Container vs. Profile Container
flashcards.back: A Profile Container carries the entire user profile. An Office Container can optionally carry just Outlook (OST/search data) and OneDrive data separately, which is useful in a hybrid setup where the main profile stays local or on a different container while Office data still roams.
flashcards.detail: Splitting Office data into its own container is mainly useful when profile size needs to be kept small or when Outlook cached-mode data would otherwise dominate the profile container.

flashcards.front: MSIX app attach: staging and de-staging
flashcards.back: At sign-in, the MSIX app attach agent stages (mounts) the application's image and registers the app for that user; at sign-out, it de-stages (unmounts) it. The app is available for the duration of the session without ever being locally installed.
flashcards.detail: Because staging happens at sign-in rather than at image build time, adding, updating, or removing an MSIX app attach application does not require touching or redeploying the session host golden image at all.

flashcards.front: FSLogix Application Masking
flashcards.back: Hides specific applications, Start menu shortcuts, or file associations from specific users or groups on a shared multi-session image, without uninstalling the application. The app is still physically present but invisible to unauthorized users.
flashcards.detail: Application Masking uses rule sets evaluated against Active Directory group membership, which is how one golden image can serve different departments each seeing only the apps licensed or relevant to them.

flashcards.front: Per-user Start menu and taskbar personalization
flashcards.back: Windows multi-session supports per-user pinned Start menu tiles and taskbar icons that roam with the user's FSLogix profile container, so each user's customizations persist across sessions and session hosts instead of everyone sharing one fixed layout.
flashcards.detail: Before this per-user taskbar capability, every user on a multi-session host shared a single, image-baked taskbar layout that no individual user could change.

flashcards.front: Installing language packs on a multi-session image
flashcards.back: Language packs and Features on Demand must be added to the master (golden) image itself, typically via DISM against a language pack/FOD ISO, before the image is generalized and used to create session hosts. They are not installed per-user after deployment the way a desktop app would be.
flashcards.detail: This is a common exam trap: language support has to be baked into the image ahead of time, unlike an MSIX-attached application which can be added dynamically per user.

flashcards.front: FSLogix Redirections.xml
flashcards.back: An FSLogix configuration file that lets an admin explicitly exclude or redirect specific folders (like a large, disposable cache folder) out of the profile container, keeping the container smaller and sign-in faster.
flashcards.detail: A common use is excluding folders such as browser caches or temp data that do not need to roam with the user and would otherwise bloat the profile container unnecessarily.

flashcards.front: User Profile Disks (UPD) vs. FSLogix Profile Containers
flashcards.back: User Profile Disks were the older, RDS-era mechanism for a roaming per-user VHD profile. FSLogix Profile Containers are the modern, Microsoft-recommended replacement for Azure Virtual Desktop, offering finer-grained control, Cloud Cache redundancy, and better sign-in performance.
flashcards.detail: Azure Virtual Desktop deployments today should use FSLogix Profile Containers, not User Profile Disks; UPD is considered legacy guidance from Remote Desktop Services on Windows Server.

flashcards.front: FSLogix at shared clinical (nursing-station) workstations
flashcards.back: A hospital publishing a pooled multi-session desktop to shared nursing-station terminals can use FSLogix Profile Containers so that whichever terminal a clinician signs into, their desktop settings, pinned EHR shortcuts, and application state follow them automatically, without needing a personally assigned VM per clinician.
flashcards.detail: This pattern avoids provisioning one expensive personal host pool VM per clinician when many clinicians only ever need a consistent, personalized session on whichever shared terminal happens to be free.

flashcards.front: Azure Monitor for Azure Virtual Desktop
flashcards.back: A purpose-built monitoring workbook and set of dashboards that surfaces host pool, session host, and connection-level diagnostics, like connection failures, session host performance, and user session counts, by querying diagnostic data sent to a Log Analytics workspace.
flashcards.detail: It requires diagnostic settings to actually be enabled on the AVD objects (host pools, workspaces, app groups) first; Azure Monitor for AVD has nothing to show until diagnostic data is flowing into a Log Analytics workspace.

flashcards.front: AVD diagnostic settings and Log Analytics categories
flashcards.back: Diagnostic settings on Azure Virtual Desktop objects can send categories like Checkpoint, Error, Management, Connection, HostRegistration, AgentHealthStatus, NetworkData, and SessionHostManagement logs to a Log Analytics workspace for querying and the Azure Monitor for AVD workbook.
flashcards.detail: Connection and Error are typically the two most useful categories for day-to-day troubleshooting of failed or slow user sign-ins.

flashcards.front: Autoscale scaling plans
flashcards.back: A scaling plan defines schedules (ramp-up, peak, ramp-down, off-peak) that automatically start or deallocate session host VMs in a host pool based on time of day and current session load, reducing compute cost outside business hours.
flashcards.detail: Autoscale needs the Azure Virtual Desktop resource provider to have the appropriate permissions (via a service-linked role) on the subscription to start and stop VMs on the plan's behalf.

flashcards.front: Drain mode
flashcards.back: Marking a session host as in drain mode prevents it from accepting any new user sessions while existing, already-connected sessions continue to run uninterrupted, used to safely empty a host before maintenance or patching.
flashcards.detail: Drain mode alone does not sign out or disconnect existing users; an admin typically also needs to message and log off remaining users, or simply wait for them to disconnect naturally, before the host is fully idle.

flashcards.front: Patching session hosts
flashcards.back: Session hosts can be patched like any Azure VM, using Azure Update Manager, Microsoft Configuration Manager, or WSUS; a common pattern is to combine drain mode with scheduled patching windows, or to replace hosts entirely with a newly patched golden image rather than patching in place.
flashcards.detail: Image-based replacement (deploy new session hosts from an updated Azure Compute Gallery image version, then remove the old hosts) avoids ever having user sessions running on a host mid-patch, at the cost of needing enough spare capacity to roll hosts in and out.

flashcards.front: Multimedia redirection (MMR)
flashcards.back: Redirects video/audio playback processing from certain supported websites to the local client device instead of decoding it on the session host, cutting session host CPU load and improving playback smoothness for the user.
flashcards.detail: This is a targeted fix for a specific bottleneck — media decoding load — distinct from the general connection-quality goal that RDP Shortpath addresses.

flashcards.front: Teams media optimization for AVD
flashcards.back: Offloads Microsoft Teams call/meeting audio, video, and screen sharing to run directly on the client device (via the Teams AVD media optimization WebRTC redirector), instead of processing that media load on the shared session host.
flashcards.detail: Without this optimization enabled, every Teams call on a multi-session host competes for the same shared session host security baselines and CPU/network resources, which degrades quickly as concurrent user count grows.

flashcards.front: Azure Virtual Desktop vs. Windows 365 decision factors
flashcards.back: AVD is a multi-session, admin-managed service billed by Azure consumption where IT controls host pool sizing, scaling, and multi-user density. Windows 365 Cloud PC is a fixed per-user, per-month priced dedicated Windows PC in the cloud with a simpler, pre-sized experience and no host pool or scaling plan to manage. Choose AVD for multi-session pooled economics and granular scaling control; choose Windows 365 for predictable per-user pricing and a simplified, dedicated PC.
flashcards.detail: Windows 365 Cloud PCs are actually provisioned on top of Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure under the hood and can even surface inside the same unified portal, but a Cloud PC can never be pooled across multiple users or scaled the way an AVD host pool can, since it is always a fixed, dedicated, single-user VM.

flashcards.front: FSLogix profile container size limits
flashcards.back: FSLogix profile containers default to a maximum size of 30 GB (the SizeInMBs setting) unless increased, and administrators should size containers based on realistic per-user profile growth rather than accepting the default blindly. The IsDynamic setting, recommended enabled, makes the VHD(X) grow only as data is actually written instead of pre-allocating its full configured size up front.
flashcards.detail: A container sized too small silently fills up and can put a user into a temporary or read-only profile with no obvious sign-in error, so proactively monitoring container free space avoids a hard-to-diagnose 'why does this one user keep losing settings' ticket.

flashcards.front: Autoscale scale-out differs for personal vs. pooled host pools
flashcards.back: On a pooled host pool, autoscale can start/stop existing session hosts and adjust how many hosts are running to match a schedule and session load. On a personal host pool, a scaling plan can only start or deallocate the fixed set of existing dedicated VMs on a schedule or on disconnect/logoff — it cannot create or remove session hosts, since each VM is permanently tied to one assigned user.
flashcards.detail: Because a personal host pool's VM count never changes, 'scaling' there really just means power state management (Start VM on Connect plus scheduled ramp-down or deallocate-on-disconnect), not the create/remove-host elasticity a pooled host pool provides.

flashcards.front: AVD control plane vs. data plane
flashcards.back: The Azure Virtual Desktop control plane — Web Access, the Broker, Diagnostics, and the Gateway — is fully managed by Microsoft and runs in Microsoft's own subscription, at no infrastructure cost to the customer. The data plane — session host VMs, the virtual network, and FSLogix storage — runs in the customer's own Azure subscription, and that is the part the customer provisions, patches, and pays for.
flashcards.detail: Because the control plane lives outside the customer's subscription and tenant boundary, a customer can never see or manage the Broker or Gateway directly in the portal; troubleshooting connection brokering issues means using AVD diagnostics and Log Analytics data, not inspecting a customer-owned resource.

flashcards.front: Session host VM sizing and capacity planning
flashcards.back: Sizing session hosts starts from an expected user profile — light, medium, or heavy, based on the applications and multitasking typical for that user group — which Microsoft documents with recommended vCPU, RAM, and users-per-core ratios per profile; the Azure Virtual Desktop Experience Estimator and published sizing tables translate expected concurrent users and workload type into a specific VM SKU and session-per-host count.
flashcards.detail: Under-sizing shows up as sluggish sessions under peak concurrent load even though the VM looks healthy at idle, so capacity planning should be validated against a pilot at real peak-hour concurrency, not just steady-state averages.

flashcards.front: Host pool maximum session limit
flashcards.back: The max session limit setting on a pooled host pool caps how many concurrent user sessions any single session host in that pool will accept, working together with the load-balancing algorithm to decide when a host is considered full and new sessions should route elsewhere (breadth-first) or a new host should be brought online (depth-first with autoscale).
flashcards.detail: Setting this limit too high for the VM's actual sizing overloads the host under peak load even though the pool still shows spare 'slots,' while setting it too low wastes capacity and forces autoscale to spin up more hosts than necessary.

flashcards.front: Azure Hybrid Benefit and cost optimization for session hosts
flashcards.back: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets an organization apply an existing on-premises Windows Server license with Software Assurance toward session host compute cost, and Reserved Instances or Azure Savings Plans can further discount predictable VM compute, both targeting AVD's largest ongoing cost driver: the session host compute itself.
flashcards.detail: Windows 10/11 multi-session VM compute is not eligible for the same per-core Hybrid Benefit discount that Windows Server workloads get, so on multi-session host pools the realistic savings levers are autoscale (avoid paying for idle capacity) and Reserved Instances/Savings Plans on compute, not Hybrid Benefit.

flashcards.front: Single sign-on (SSO) for AVD sessions
flashcards.back: Azure Virtual Desktop can provide single sign-on so a user who already signed in with Windows Hello for Business, a FIDO2 key, or another passwordless method is not prompted for credentials again when connecting to a session host, using either Microsoft Entra Kerberos-based SSO or certificate-based authentication issued dynamically at connection time.
flashcards.detail: SSO is a host pool-level setting configured in addition to Conditional Access, and it specifically targets the second, in-session authentication prompt a user otherwise sees even after already completing MFA once to reach the feed — without it, users can be prompted for credentials twice for what feels like one sign-in.

flashcards.front: Desktop Virtualization Power On Off Contributor role
flashcards.back: A built-in RBAC role that grants only the rights to start and stop (power on/off) session host VMs, without any broader Virtual Machine Contributor rights like resizing or deleting VMs; it is the role assigned to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal so autoscale scaling plans and Start VM on Connect can power hosts on and off on the customer's behalf.
flashcards.detail: Granting this narrower role instead of full Virtual Machine Contributor to the AVD service principal follows least privilege — the automation that starts and stops VMs for scaling has no ability to resize, delete, or reconfigure them.

flashcards.front: Restricting session host network exposure
flashcards.back: Session hosts should have no public IP address and should never be directly reachable for inbound RDP from the internet; all user connections are brokered through the AVD Gateway over an outbound-only connection from the session host, so network security groups can safely deny all unsolicited inbound RDP while the reverse-connect transport the service needs still works.
flashcards.detail: Because the session host always initiates an outbound connection to the AVD infrastructure rather than listening for inbound internet connections, admins do not need to open any inbound internet-facing RDP port on the session host's NSG at all — a common misconception carried over from traditional on-premises RDS deployments.

flashcards.front: Printer redirection in AVD sessions
flashcards.back: The Remote Desktop Easy Print driver redirects a user's local, client-side printers into the remote session automatically without needing that specific printer's driver installed on the session host, while universal print redirection can alternatively route print jobs through Universal Print, Microsoft's cloud-based print service, instead of relying on client-side printer redirection at all.
flashcards.detail: Easy Print can be slow or fail with printers that have unusual custom drivers or many options, in which case installing the vendor driver directly on the golden image (true driver redirection) is the fallback, at the cost of having to keep that driver updated on the image.

flashcards.front: GPU-accelerated session hosts
flashcards.back: For graphics-intensive workloads such as CAD, 3D modeling, or video editing, session hosts can run on Azure GPU-enabled VM sizes (such as the NV-series) with either GPU passthrough for a dedicated hardware GPU or GPU partitioning/vGPU for sharing one physical GPU across multiple session hosts, combined with an appropriate GPU driver installed in the image.
flashcards.detail: A pooled multi-session host pool running heavy graphics workloads on a GPU-enabled SKU still shares that one GPU's capacity across every concurrent session on the host, so GPU-bound capacity planning matters just as much as vCPU/RAM sizing for this workload type.

flashcards.front: Deploying Win32 apps via Intune vs. MSIX app attach
flashcards.back: Microsoft Intune can deploy traditional Win32 application installers to session hosts the same way it does to any managed Windows endpoint, installing the app directly into the OS the same for every user, whereas MSIX app attach dynamically attaches an MSIX-packaged app per user at sign-in with nothing installed into the OS. Intune Win32 deployment fits apps needed by every user of a host pool, while MSIX app attach fits apps assignable to specific users or groups without touching the image.
flashcards.detail: An application that is not available as an MSIX package (many legacy line-of-business installers) has no MSIX app attach option at all, so Intune Win32 deployment or baking it into the golden image are the only realistic delivery paths for it.

flashcards.front: Enforcing a default Start menu/taskbar layout via Group Policy
flashcards.back: A Start layout XML file exported from a reference machine can be imported through Group Policy or an Intune configuration profile to lock in a specific default set of pinned Start menu tiles and taskbar icons for every new user profile on a multi-session image, distinct from the per-user personalization that individual users can later customize and roam via FSLogix.
flashcards.detail: A fully locked, non-customizable layout and a merely default, user-editable layout are two different GPO options — pushing a fully locked layout also blocks the per-user Start/taskbar personalization that FSLogix would otherwise roam for that user, so admins must choose one behavior or the other, not both.

flashcards.front: Querying AVD connection data with KQL
flashcards.back: The WVDConnections table in Log Analytics records each session's connection lifecycle (such as Connected and Completed states) plus duration and round-trip time, while WVDCheckpoints records the timestamped stages a connection passed through, letting an admin write a Kusto Query Language (KQL) query to pinpoint exactly which stage — client, gateway, broker, or session host — a specific failed or slow connection stalled at.
flashcards.detail: Filtering WVDConnections by UserName or CorrelationId is the fastest way to trace one specific user's reported bad connection, rather than scanning the prebuilt Azure Monitor for AVD workbook visuals for an issue affecting only a single person.

flashcards.front: Scheduled agent updates for session hosts
flashcards.back: The Azure Virtual Desktop agent and side-by-side stack on session hosts update automatically by default, but the scheduled agent updates feature lets an admin define a specific maintenance window (day and time) during which those automatic updates are allowed to install, keeping unexpected agent restarts out of business hours.
flashcards.detail: This controls only the AVD agent/side-by-side stack itself, not Windows OS updates or application patching, which still need to be managed separately through Azure Update Manager, WSUS, Configuration Manager, or golden-image replacement.

questions.question: A company wants a cost-efficient desktop solution where many employees performing similar, non-persistent tasks share a pool of Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session VMs, with no need for per-user persistent local customization on the VM itself. Which host pool type fits?
options: A pooled host pool
A personal host pool with automatic assignment
A personal host pool with direct assignment
A pooled host pool configured for one dedicated VM per user
questions.explanation: A pooled host pool is designed for exactly this: many non-persistent users sharing multi-session VMs load-balanced across the pool, keeping costs down since VMs are shared rather than dedicated. Personal host pools dedicate one VM per user, which does not fit a shared, non-persistent scenario.

questions.question: An administrator wants new user sessions concentrated onto as few session hosts as possible during off-peak hours, so that autoscale can safely deallocate the emptied hosts to save cost. Which load-balancing algorithm should the pooled host pool use?
options: Breadth-first
Depth-first
Round-robin across all regions
Least recently used
questions.explanation: Depth-first fills each session host to its configured maximum session limit before moving on to the next host, concentrating sessions and leaving other hosts empty and available for autoscale to deallocate. Breadth-first instead spreads sessions evenly across every host, working against that consolidation goal.

questions.question: A host pool currently publishes a Desktop application group to a group of users. An administrator also wants to publish a RemoteApp for a single line-of-business application from that same host pool to the same users. What should the administrator consider?
options: This configuration is impossible; a host pool can only have one application group total
RemoteApp application groups can only be created on personal host pools

Publishing both a RemoteApp and a Desktop app group from the same host pool to the same users is technically possible but not recommended, since it can cause duplicate application icons and user confusion
The Desktop application group must first be deleted before any RemoteApp group can be added
questions.explanation: A pooled host pool can have multiple application groups, including a Desktop app group and one or more RemoteApp groups, but Microsoft specifically recommends against assigning the same users both a RemoteApp and a Desktop app group from the same host pool due to icon duplication and confusion. It is not technically blocked, just discouraged.

questions.question: A team wants to build, version, and roll out custom Windows 11 multi-session session host images across two Azure regions with the ability to test a new version in a small validation host pool before wider release. Which service should they use to manage the images?
options: Azure Container Registry
Azure Files Premium
Azure Backup vault
Azure Compute Gallery
questions.explanation: Azure Compute Gallery stores, versions, and replicates custom VM images across regions and subscriptions, which is exactly what is needed to manage and progressively roll out session host image versions. The other services address container images, file storage, and backup, not VM image versioning.

questions.question: A large enterprise AVD deployment needs the lowest possible storage latency for FSLogix profile containers at very high user scale, and the team is willing to manage a dedicated delegated subnet for it. Which storage option best fits?
options: Azure NetApp Files
Azure Files (Standard tier)
A single local disk on each session host
Azure Blob Storage (Cool tier)
questions.explanation: Azure NetApp Files offers the lowest latency and highest throughput/IOPS of the listed FSLogix storage options, making it the recommended choice at large scale, at the cost of extra setup like a delegated subnet. A local disk on each host cannot be shared across session hosts, which FSLogix profile storage requires, and Blob Storage does not support SMB file shares for VHD(X) containers.

questions.question: Remote Desktop clients connect to session hosts over a corporate VPN with direct network line-of-sight to the Azure virtual network. The company wants to minimize round-trip latency by avoiding the usual relay through the Remote Desktop Gateway. What should be enabled?
options: RDP Shortpath for public networks
RDP Shortpath for managed networks
Azure Front Door
Azure Bastion
questions.explanation: RDP Shortpath for managed networks establishes a direct UDP transport between client and session host when there is direct line-of-sight connectivity, such as over a VPN or ExpressRoute, bypassing the Gateway relay. RDP Shortpath for public networks is instead meant for clients with no such direct connectivity, using STUN/TURN-based NAT traversal.

questions.question: An administrator is planning FSLogix storage locations and wants the greatest resilience if one storage location becomes temporarily unreachable, by writing profile changes locally first and asynchronously replicating them to multiple storage providers. Which FSLogix capability should be configured?
options: Application Masking
Redirections.xml
Cloud Cache
Office Container only, with no Profile Container
questions.explanation: Cloud Cache writes to a local cache first and asynchronously replicates to one or more configured storage providers, giving resilience against any single storage location being unavailable. Application Masking and Redirections.xml solve different problems: hiding apps and excluding folders, respectively.

questions.question: A host pool administrator wants to test an upcoming Azure Virtual Desktop service and agent update on a small number of session hosts before it reaches the organization's production host pools. What should be configured on that small host pool?
options: Enable drain mode on every session host in the pool
Set the load-balancing algorithm to depth-first
Create a new Azure Compute Gallery image definition
Enable the 'Validation environment' setting on the host pool
questions.explanation: A host pool flagged as a validation environment receives Azure Virtual Desktop service and agent updates ahead of production host pools, letting admins catch update-related issues on a small, low-risk pool first. The other options do not affect which update ring a host pool belongs to.

questions.question: A company's end users need to see one unified feed containing every application and desktop they are entitled to, spanning several host pools and application groups, when they open the Remote Desktop client. What should be published to them?
options: A workspace containing the relevant application groups
A single application group directly, with no workspace involved
A single host pool resource, with no application groups
A Log Analytics workspace
questions.explanation: A workspace is the logical container that groups multiple application groups together for publishing, giving users one unified feed across everything they are assigned. A Log Analytics workspace is an unrelated monitoring resource with a similar name, a common exam distractor.

questions.question: A finance director requires a dedicated virtual desktop that keeps locally installed line-of-business software and manual customizations intact between sessions, and wants IT to pre-assign that specific VM to the director ahead of their first sign-in. Which configuration fits?
options: A pooled host pool with breadth-first load balancing
A personal host pool with direct assignment
A personal host pool with automatic assignment
A RemoteApp application group only
questions.explanation: Direct assignment on a personal host pool lets an admin pre-assign a specific session host VM to a specific user before their first connection, preserving a persistent, dedicated desktop. Automatic assignment instead only assigns a VM the first time the user connects, not ahead of time.

questions.question: During a network readiness assessment for a new Azure Virtual Desktop deployment, an admin measures round-trip time (RTT) between a branch office and the target Azure region. Which factor does high RTT primarily degrade?
options: The maximum number of MSIX packages that can be attached
The FSLogix container's maximum file size
The interactive responsiveness the user perceives during their session
The number of RBAC roles that can be assigned
questions.explanation: Round-trip time between the client and the session host's region is the dominant factor in how responsive an interactive remote session feels; high RTT causes noticeable input and screen-update lag regardless of available bandwidth. It has no relationship to MSIX package limits, container size limits, or RBAC role counts.

questions.question: An organization wants to publish a line-of-business application via MSIX app attach and needs a location the session hosts can reach to retrieve the MSIX image at sign-in. What is commonly used to host that MSIX image?
options: A local folder on each session host's C: drive
The Azure Compute Gallery image definition
A Conditional Access policy
A network file share, such as an SMB share on Azure Files
questions.explanation: MSIX app attach images are typically staged on a network share (commonly an Azure Files SMB share) that every session host in the pool can reach, so the app can be dynamically attached to any host a user lands on. A local per-host folder would not be reachable by other hosts in the pool, breaking the pooled, stateless model.

questions.question: A company deploys Microsoft Entra-joined session hosts with no on-premises Active Directory at all, and wants FSLogix profile containers stored on Azure Files using Kerberos authentication rather than a storage account key. What must be configured to make this possible?
options: Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication for the Azure Files storage account
Hybrid Entra join for every session host
A Conditional Access policy targeting the storage account
Application Masking rule sets
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Kerberos for Azure Files lets Entra-joined-only devices, with no on-premises AD at all, authenticate to an Azure Files share with Kerberos, enabling FSLogix on a purely cloud-native identity setup. Hybrid Entra join would instead require an on-premises AD DS domain, which this scenario does not have.

questions.question: An administrator needs to grant a help-desk technician the ability to disable new connections to a specific session host and send it a maintenance message, but without letting that technician delete host pools or application groups. Which built-in role fits best?
options: Desktop Virtualization Contributor
Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator
Desktop Virtualization User
Owner
questions.explanation: Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator is scoped specifically to session host operations like enabling/disabling new connections and sending messages, without the broader object-management rights of Desktop Virtualization Contributor. Desktop Virtualization User only grants end-user access to app groups, not admin actions.

questions.question: A company wants to require multi-factor authentication before any user, including one connecting through the native Remote Desktop client using the RDP protocol, can start an Azure Virtual Desktop session. Which Microsoft Entra enterprise apps should the Conditional Access policy target?
options: Only the Azure Virtual Desktop app
Only the Windows Cloud Login app
The Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows Cloud Login apps together
Only the Microsoft 365 admin center app
questions.explanation: Both the Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows Cloud Login enterprise apps typically need to be targeted together for Conditional Access to be enforced consistently across the web client and the RDP protocol's own authentication step used by the native client. Targeting only one of the two can leave a gap for the other.

questions.question: A hospital wants to prevent clinical staff from taking screenshots of sensitive patient data displayed inside their Azure Virtual Desktop session using third-party screen-capture tools running on the client device. Which RDP property should be enabled?
options: Watermarking only
Drain mode
Breadth-first load balancing
Screen capture protection
questions.explanation: Screen capture protection actively blocks a session's content from being captured by screenshot or screen-recording tools on the client, which directly addresses the described concern. Watermarking only deters by visibly marking the session; it does not technically block a capture the way screen capture protection does.

questions.question: An administrator is hardening a set of session hosts and wants to apply Microsoft's published, AVD-specific security recommendations, including redirection restrictions and RDP listener hardening, consistently across every host. What is the recommended way to apply these?
options: Apply the Azure Virtual Desktop security baseline through Group Policy or Intune settings catalog policies
Manually configure each setting by hand on every session host after deployment
Enable screen capture protection only
Rely on the default Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session settings with no changes
questions.explanation: Applying the published security baseline through Group Policy or Intune settings catalog policies is the supported, scalable way to harden every session host consistently. Manually configuring each host by hand does not scale and is error-prone across a fleet of session hosts.

questions.question: An organization needs Japanese-language support available to users on a Windows 11 multi-session host pool. When should the Japanese language pack be installed?
options: After each user signs in for the first time, via Windows Update
Into the master image, before it is generalized and used to create session hosts
Automatically, the first time a Japanese-language document is opened
Only on personal host pools, never on pooled host pools
questions.explanation: Language packs and Features on Demand must be added to the master image itself before it is generalized and deployed, since they are not something Azure Virtual Desktop installs per-user automatically after the fact. Multi-session pooled host pools support language packs the same way personal host pools do, provided they are baked into the image.

questions.question: A shared multi-session image includes a licensed finance application that only the finance department should be able to see and launch; other departments share the same image but must not see it in their Start menu at all. What FSLogix feature addresses this without maintaining a separate image per department?
options: Cloud Cache
Redirections.xml
Application Masking
Screen capture protection
questions.explanation: Application Masking hides an installed application from unauthorized users or groups based on rule sets, without uninstalling it or requiring a separate image, exactly fitting a single shared image serving multiple departments. Cloud Cache and Redirections.xml address storage redundancy and folder exclusions, not visibility of applications.

questions.question: A profile container is growing unexpectedly large because of a browser cache folder that does not need to roam between sessions. What is the recommended way to keep that folder out of the FSLogix profile container?
options: Uninstall the browser entirely from the image
Switch from Profile Containers to User Profile Disks
Disable FSLogix entirely for that user
Configure an exclusion for that folder in FSLogix's Redirections.xml
questions.explanation: Redirections.xml lets an admin explicitly exclude specific folders, like a disposable browser cache, from the profile container, keeping it smaller without removing the underlying application. Disabling FSLogix or switching to the legacy User Profile Disk mechanism would be a far more disruptive overcorrection.

questions.question: A team wants to publish a frequently updated line-of-business application to Azure Virtual Desktop users while minimizing how often the golden image itself needs to be rebuilt and redeployed for application updates. Which approach best achieves this?
options: Package the application as MSIX and deliver it via MSIX app attach
Install the application directly into the golden image and redeploy the image for every update
Publish it only as a RemoteApp with the application still installed in the image
Disable autoscale so session hosts never restart
questions.explanation: MSIX app attach dynamically attaches the packaged application at sign-in without installing it in the golden image, so updating the application is just adding a new package version rather than rebuilding and redeploying the image. Installing directly into the image ties every app update to a full image lifecycle.

questions.question: A hybrid organization wants Outlook cached-mode and OneDrive data to roam with the user, but keeps the rest of the profile intentionally small and separately managed. Which FSLogix container should specifically be configured for the Outlook/OneDrive data?
options: Profile Container only
Office Container
Cloud Cache with no Profile Container
Application Masking rule set
questions.explanation: The Office Container is specifically designed to carry Outlook and OneDrive data separately from the main Profile Container, which fits a scenario that wants that data roaming while keeping overall profile size and management separate. Application Masking has nothing to do with roaming data.

questions.question: Two different users sign in at different times to the same Windows 11 multi-session session host and each wants their own personally pinned Start menu tiles and taskbar icons to appear, rather than a single shared, image-baked layout for everyone. What makes this possible?
options: Application Masking rule sets
RDP Shortpath for managed networks
Per-user Start menu and taskbar personalization roaming with the FSLogix profile container
Depth-first load balancing
questions.explanation: Windows multi-session's per-user Start menu and taskbar personalization roams with each user's FSLogix profile container, so each user keeps their own layout regardless of which session host they land on. The other options concern app visibility, network transport, and session distribution, not personalized UI layout.

questions.question: A hospital deploys a pooled multi-session host pool for shared nursing-station terminals, where any clinician might sign in at any terminal during a shift. Which combination best ensures each clinician's personal desktop settings and pinned EHR shortcuts follow them to whichever terminal they use?
options: A personal host pool with one dedicated VM assigned to each clinician
A pooled host pool with no profile management configured
MSIX app attach alone, with no FSLogix configured
A pooled host pool with FSLogix Profile Containers
questions.explanation: A pooled host pool combined with FSLogix Profile Containers lets each clinician's settings and shortcuts roam with them to any shared terminal, without the cost of dedicating a VM per clinician. Leaving profile management unconfigured would reset each clinician to a blank profile on every new terminal.

questions.question: An administrator wants to see connection failures, session host performance, and active session counts for a host pool in a prebuilt dashboard. What must first be configured before Azure Monitor for Azure Virtual Desktop has any data to show?
options: Diagnostic settings sending AVD diagnostic categories to a Log Analytics workspace
Drain mode on every session host
A Conditional Access policy on the host pool
An Azure Compute Gallery image definition
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor for AVD's workbook queries diagnostic data in a Log Analytics workspace, so diagnostic settings must be enabled on the relevant AVD objects first, or the workbook has nothing to display. The other options do not feed data into Azure Monitor for AVD at all.

questions.question: An admin troubleshooting a spike in failed user sign-ins wants to review the most relevant Log Analytics diagnostic category for connection-level failures. Which category should they query first?
options: AgentHealthStatus
Connection
NetworkData
SessionHostManagement
questions.explanation: The Connection diagnostic category logs connection-level events, including failures during sign-in, making it the most directly relevant category for this kind of troubleshooting. AgentHealthStatus, NetworkData, and SessionHostManagement cover different aspects of the environment, not connection failure detail.

questions.question: A company wants session host VMs to automatically start during business hours and deallocate overnight and on weekends to control cost, without manual intervention each day. What should be configured on the host pool?
options: Drain mode on all hosts permanently
Direct assignment on every session host
A scaling plan (autoscale)
Application Masking rule sets
questions.explanation: A scaling plan (autoscale) defines schedules like ramp-up, peak, ramp-down, and off-peak that automatically start and deallocate session hosts based on time of day and load, exactly matching the described automatic cost control. Drain mode only stops new sessions; it does not start or deallocate VMs on a schedule.

questions.question: Before applying a critical security patch to a pooled host pool's session hosts, an admin wants to stop new users from landing on a specific host while letting its currently connected users finish their work undisturbed. What should the admin do to that host first?
options: Delete the session host from the host pool
Disable the host pool's workspace
Switch the load-balancing algorithm to breadth-first
Enable drain mode on the session host
questions.explanation: Enabling drain mode on a session host stops it from accepting new sessions while letting existing connected sessions continue uninterrupted, which is exactly the safe pre-patching step described. Deleting the host would forcibly disconnect existing users, and disabling the workspace would affect every host pool published through it.

questions.question: Personal host pools support a load-balancing algorithm selection, the same as pooled host pools.
questions.explanation: Load-balancing algorithms (breadth-first and depth-first) apply only to pooled host pools, since a personal host pool already maps each user to one specific, dedicated session host with no load to balance across multiple hosts.

questions.question: A host pool's session hosts can run either Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session or Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session.
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop supports both Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session and Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session as valid session host operating systems, alongside single-session Windows client and Windows Server options.

questions.question: Azure NetApp Files requires its own delegated subnet within the virtual network.
questions.explanation: Azure NetApp Files volumes are provisioned into a subnet that must be delegated specifically to the Microsoft.NetApp/volumes resource, which is additional network setup that a standard Azure Files share does not require.

questions.question: RDP Shortpath for public networks relies on STUN/TURN-based techniques to establish a direct connection even when the client has no direct line-of-sight to the session host's virtual network.
questions.explanation: RDP Shortpath for public networks specifically targets clients without direct network line-of-sight, such as home users on the open internet, using STUN/TURN-style NAT traversal, distinct from RDP Shortpath for managed networks which assumes direct connectivity like a VPN.

questions.question: Azure Compute Gallery image definitions can be replicated across multiple Azure regions from a single gallery.
questions.explanation: One of Azure Compute Gallery's key benefits is replicating image versions across multiple regions and subscriptions from a single, centrally managed gallery, rather than manually copying managed images region by region.

questions.question: A Microsoft Entra-joined session host, with no on-premises Active Directory at all, can never support FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files.
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication for Azure Files specifically enables FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files for Entra-joined-only session hosts with no on-premises AD, so this scenario is fully supported today, not impossible.

questions.question: Watermarking technically prevents a user from capturing session content with a screenshot tool, the same way screen capture protection does.
questions.explanation: Watermarking only overlays deterrent information on the session; it does not technically block a capture attempt the way screen capture protection actively does. They serve complementary, not identical, purposes.

questions.question: MSIX app attach applications are installed directly onto the session host's local disk at sign-in, just like a traditional MSI installer.
questions.explanation: MSIX app attach applications are staged as a virtual disk and attached to the session, never actually installed onto the local disk. That is precisely what avoids modifying the golden image or local storage.

questions.question: FSLogix Application Masking can hide an installed application from specific users or groups without uninstalling it from the shared image.
questions.explanation: Application Masking evaluates rule sets against group membership to hide (mask) an application's visibility for unauthorized users, while the application remains physically installed on the shared image for everyone else.

questions.question: Language packs delivered through MSIX app attach can be installed per-user after sign-in on a multi-session host, without touching the master image.
questions.explanation: Language packs must be baked into the master image before it is generalized and deployed. MSIX app attach is for delivering applications dynamically, not for delivering language pack functionality per user.

questions.question: The FSLogix Office Container can be configured to roam separately from the main Profile Container.
questions.explanation: The Office Container is a distinct, separately configurable container specifically for Outlook and OneDrive data, which can be managed and stored apart from the main Profile Container.

questions.question: Drain mode automatically signs out every currently connected user on a session host as soon as it is enabled.
questions.explanation: Drain mode only blocks new sessions from landing on that host; existing, already-connected sessions continue running until the users disconnect or sign out on their own, or are explicitly logged off by an admin.

questions.question: A scaling plan (autoscale) requires the Azure Virtual Desktop service to have permission to start and deallocate session host VMs on the subscription's behalf.
questions.explanation: Autoscale relies on a service-linked role granting the Azure Virtual Desktop resource provider permission to start and deallocate VMs according to the scaling plan's schedule; without that permission, autoscale cannot act on the host pool's VMs.

questions.question: Which two of the following are valid Azure Virtual Desktop load-balancing algorithms for a pooled host pool? (Choose two.)
options: Breadth-first
Depth-first
Round-robin
Least connections
questions.explanation: Breadth-first and depth-first are the two load-balancing algorithms Azure Virtual Desktop actually offers for pooled host pools. Round-robin and least connections are generic load-balancer terms from other products, not options exposed for AVD host pools.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about personal host pools? (Choose two.)
options: They use breadth-first or depth-first load balancing to distribute sessions
They support automatic or direct user assignment
Each session host is dedicated to exactly one assigned user
They support unlimited concurrent users per session host
questions.explanation: Personal host pools support automatic or direct assignment, and each session host is dedicated to exactly one assigned user. Unlike a pooled host pool, they do not use breadth-first/depth-first load balancing since there is no session distribution decision to make, and they certainly do not support unlimited concurrent users per host.

questions.question: Which two of the following are genuine benefits of using Azure Compute Gallery for session host images? (Choose two.)
options: Automatically installing FSLogix on every session host
Automatically applying Conditional Access policies to new VMs
Versioning images so a new build can be tested before wider rollout
Replicating an image across multiple Azure regions
questions.explanation: Azure Compute Gallery's core value is image versioning and multi-region replication for controlled rollout. It has nothing to do with automatically installing FSLogix or applying Conditional Access policies, which are separate configuration and identity concerns.

questions.question: Which two of the following statements about RDP Shortpath are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: RDP Shortpath for managed networks requires direct line-of-sight connectivity such as a VPN or ExpressRoute
RDP Shortpath always requires the Remote Desktop Gateway to relay every packet
RDP Shortpath is only available for personal host pools, never pooled host pools
RDP Shortpath for public networks uses STUN/TURN-based NAT traversal
questions.explanation: RDP Shortpath for managed networks needs direct line-of-sight connectivity, and RDP Shortpath for public networks uses STUN/TURN NAT traversal for clients without that direct connectivity. Its entire purpose is to establish a direct UDP path that avoids relaying through the Gateway, and it applies to both personal and pooled host pools equally.

questions.question: Which two of the following are built-in Azure Virtual Desktop RBAC roles? (Choose two.)
options: Desktop Virtualization User
Remote Desktop Gateway Administrator
Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator
Virtual Desktop Global Reader
questions.explanation: Desktop Virtualization User and Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator are both genuine built-in Azure Virtual Desktop RBAC roles. The other two option names are not real Azure Virtual Desktop built-in roles.

questions.question: Which two controls specifically help protect sensitive on-screen session content from being captured or photographed by a user? (Choose two.)
options: Drain mode
Screen capture protection
Autoscale scaling plans
Watermarking
questions.explanation: Screen capture protection technically blocks capture attempts, and watermarking deters capture/photography by visibly marking the session with identifying information. Both are aimed at protecting sensitive on-screen content. Drain mode and autoscale address session host availability and cost, not content protection.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about MSIX app attach? (Choose two.)
options: The application is staged as a virtual disk and attached to the session at sign-in
Updating the application generally does not require rebuilding the golden image
The application must be installed into the golden image before deployment
It uninstalls Application Masking rule sets automatically
questions.explanation: MSIX app attach stages the app as a virtual disk at sign-in without installing it into the image, so updates are handled by adding a new package version rather than rebuilding the image. It has no install-into-image requirement and no relationship to Application Masking rule sets.

questions.question: Which two of the following are genuine FSLogix container types? (Choose two.)
options: Registry Container
Profile Container
Office Container
Network Container
questions.explanation: Profile Container and Office Container are the two genuine FSLogix container types. 'Registry Container' and 'Network Container' are not real FSLogix container types.

questions.question: Which two of the following are legitimate ways to patch Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts? (Choose two.)
options: Enable drain mode permanently instead of ever patching
Disable the workspace so patches apply automatically
Deploy new session hosts from an updated, patched golden image and retire the old hosts
Patch hosts in place using Azure Update Manager or a tool like WSUS/Configuration Manager
questions.explanation: Both image-based replacement (deploy new patched hosts, retire old ones) and in-place patching via Azure Update Manager or WSUS/Configuration Manager are legitimate, commonly used approaches to keeping session hosts patched. Drain mode and disabling a workspace do not patch anything by themselves.

questions.question: A company has already assigned Microsoft 365 E3 licenses, which include the required underlying Windows license rights, to every user who will access Azure Virtual Desktop. Beyond the cost of the underlying Azure infrastructure (VMs, storage, networking), what additional Azure Virtual Desktop-specific per-user license must be purchased for those users to access their published desktops?
options: A separate Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access license, purchased in addition to Microsoft 365 E3
An Azure Virtual Desktop license is required only for users on personal host pools, not pooled host pools
An Azure Virtual Desktop license is required only for external guest users, never internal employees
No separate Azure Virtual Desktop access license is required; a qualifying Windows or Microsoft 365 license already grants the user access entitlement
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop itself has no separate per-user service license; a qualifying Windows or Microsoft 365 license (such as Microsoft 365 E3) already grants the user entitlement to access Azure Virtual Desktop, and the organization only pays for the underlying Azure infrastructure it consumes. There is no distinction in this licensing model between pooled and personal host pools, or between internal and external users, that would require an extra Azure Virtual Desktop-specific license.

questions.question: A personal host pool is used by analysts who connect only a few times per week. The team wants each analyst's dedicated VM to stay deallocated when unused and automatically start the moment that analyst attempts to connect, without an admin manually starting it first and without defining a fixed daily scaling plan schedule. Which feature fits?
options: Start VM on Connect
A scaling plan with a fixed ramp-up schedule
Breadth-first load balancing
Drain mode
questions.explanation: Start VM on Connect automatically powers on a deallocated session host the moment a user attempts to connect to it, which is exactly what a personal host pool with unpredictable, occasional usage needs, without requiring a fixed time-based scaling plan schedule. A scaling plan schedule instead starts and stops VMs at predetermined times regardless of when a specific user tries to connect, while breadth-first and drain mode address session distribution and pre-maintenance host draining, not powering on a stopped VM.

questions.question: A field technician needs to connect to their published Azure Virtual Desktop desktop from a personal Android tablet, but company policy does not allow installing a dedicated Remote Desktop client app on personal, unmanaged devices. Which access method still lets them connect?
options: MSIX app attach, installed directly on the tablet
RDP Shortpath for managed networks
The Remote Desktop web client, accessed through a supported browser
A validation environment host pool
questions.explanation: The Remote Desktop web client lets a user connect to their published resources from any supported browser, with no dedicated client app installed on the device, which fits an unmanaged personal tablet where installing an app is not allowed. MSIX app attach delivers applications to session hosts rather than providing client-side connectivity, RDP Shortpath is a transport optimization for an already-connecting client, and a validation environment host pool is only an update-rollout designation, unrelated to client access method.

questions.question: An administrator wants each pooled session host's local Administrator account password automatically randomized and rotated on a schedule, stored securely in Microsoft Entra ID, instead of every session host sharing the same static local admin password that IT tracks by hand.
options: FSLogix Application Masking
Session watermarking
RDP Shortpath for managed networks
Windows LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution)
questions.explanation: Windows LAPS automatically randomizes and rotates a managed local administrator account's password on a defined schedule and stores it securely, removing the risk of every session host sharing one static, manually tracked local admin password. Application Masking, watermarking, and RDP Shortpath address application visibility, screen-content deterrence, and network transport respectively, none of which manage local admin credentials.

questions.question: A compliance requirement states that users connecting to a specific host pool must never be able to redirect their local hard drives into the remote session, preventing them from copying session data onto local storage. Which setting should be configured?
options: A custom RDP property on the host pool disabling drive redirection
Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator role assignment
FSLogix Redirections.xml
A validation environment flag on the host pool
questions.explanation: Custom RDP properties configured on the host pool, such as disabling drive redirection, directly control which local resources are allowed to redirect into the remote session. The Session Host Operator role governs administrative permissions rather than session redirection behavior, Redirections.xml controls which folders are excluded from the FSLogix profile container instead, and the validation environment flag only affects which update ring a host pool receives.

questions.question: Users report choppy audio and blurry video during Microsoft Teams calls inside their Azure Virtual Desktop session, because the session host itself is having to encode and decode all the audio and video locally rather than offloading that work to the user's own device. What should be enabled?
options: MSIX app attach for the Teams application
Media optimization for Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop
FSLogix Application Masking for Teams
Depth-first load balancing
questions.explanation: Media optimization for Microsoft Teams redirects audio and video processing to run locally on the client device instead of on the session host, which directly resolves choppy audio and video caused by the session host handling all that encoding and decoding itself. MSIX app attach only changes how the Teams application is delivered, not where media is processed, while Application Masking and the load-balancing algorithm address application visibility and session distribution, not media performance.

questions.question: An autoscale scaling plan's ramp-up phase should start an additional session host once the currently running hosts reach 80% of their combined session capacity, rather than waiting until they are completely full. Which scaling plan setting controls this?
options: The load-balancing algorithm
MinimumNumberOfRDSH
The capacity threshold percentage
Drain mode
questions.explanation: The capacity threshold percentage is the scaling plan setting that determines what percentage of combined session capacity across running hosts triggers starting an additional host, letting ramp-up react before hosts are completely full. The load-balancing algorithm decides how sessions are distributed once hosts are already running, MinimumNumberOfRDSH sets a floor on host count rather than a utilization trigger, and drain mode only stops new sessions on one host manually.

questions.question: Azure Virtual Desktop does not require a separate, dedicated per-user Azure Virtual Desktop access license; a qualifying Windows or Microsoft 365 license plus the underlying Azure infrastructure costs are sufficient.
questions.explanation: This is accurate: Azure Virtual Desktop access itself has no separate per-user service license requirement beyond holding a qualifying Windows or Microsoft 365 license, on top of paying for the Azure infrastructure (VMs, storage, networking) actually consumed.

questions.question: Enabling media optimization for Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop causes audio and video processing to occur locally on the client device rather than on the session host.
questions.explanation: That is precisely what media optimization for Teams does: it offloads audio and video encoding and decoding to the local client device instead of the session host, improving call quality and reducing session host load.

questions.question: The Azure Monitor for Azure Virtual Desktop workbook must be built entirely from scratch by an administrator, since Microsoft provides no premade workbook template for it.
questions.explanation: Microsoft provides a premade Azure Monitor for Azure Virtual Desktop workbook template that an administrator installs and points at their Log Analytics workspace; it does not need to be built from scratch, though it can be customized further once deployed.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about hardening local administrator access and session behavior on Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts? (Choose two.)
options: Windows LAPS can automatically randomize and rotate the local Administrator account password on session hosts
Watermarking technically blocks a user from capturing session content with a screenshot tool
Custom RDP properties configured on a host pool can disable local drive redirection into the session
FSLogix Application Masking hides the RDP listener from unauthorized users
questions.explanation: Windows LAPS automatically rotates and secures the local administrator password on session hosts, and custom RDP properties on a host pool can disable local drive redirection into the session. Watermarking only deters capture visually rather than technically blocking it, which is screen capture protection's job instead, and Application Masking hides applications from users, not the RDP listener itself.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about client connectivity and Microsoft Teams optimization on Azure Virtual Desktop? (Choose two.)
options: MSIX app attach must be configured before Teams media optimization will function at all
The Remote Desktop web client lets a user connect to published resources from a supported browser with no dedicated client app installed
The Windows Desktop client is only available for Windows operating systems, with no client for macOS, iOS, or Android
Enabling media optimization for Microsoft Teams offloads audio and video processing to the local client device
questions.explanation: The Remote Desktop web client provides browser-based access with no app installed, and Teams media optimization offloads audio and video processing to the local client device. Teams media optimization has no dependency on MSIX app attach, and Microsoft provides Remote Desktop clients for macOS, iOS, and Android in addition to Windows, not just Windows.

questions.question: An organization wants predictable, fixed per-user monthly pricing for a dedicated cloud PC with no host pool sizing or scaling plan to manage, and does not need to pool multiple users onto shared multi-session hardware. Which service best fits this requirement?
options: Azure Virtual Desktop with a pooled host pool
Windows 365 Cloud PC
Azure Virtual Desktop with a personal host pool and no scaling plan
A RemoteApp application group
questions.explanation: Windows 365 Cloud PC offers fixed, predictable per-user monthly pricing and a simplified, pre-sized dedicated PC without any host pool, scaling plan, or load-balancing configuration for admins to manage. An Azure Virtual Desktop personal host pool can also dedicate one VM per user, but it is still billed on Azure consumption and still requires the admin to build and manage the host pool and its VMs directly.

questions.question: An admin reviews FSLogix Profile Container settings and notices the SizeInMBs value was left at its default. Users with unusually large profiles have begun reporting they can no longer save files or settings correctly. What is the most likely cause?
options: The default 30 GB maximum container size has been reached
IsDynamic was set to true, capping the container permanently
The container was configured as VHDX instead of VHD
Cloud Cache was enabled with two storage providers
questions.explanation: FSLogix profile containers default to a 30 GB maximum size, and once a user's container fills up they can be forced into a temporary or read-only profile with no obvious sign-in error, matching symptoms of being unable to save. IsDynamic only controls whether space is allocated as needed rather than up front, and it does not cap the container's configured maximum size.

questions.question: An administrator applies a scaling plan to a personal host pool expecting it to add new session hosts automatically when demand rises during peak hours, the way it would on a pooled host pool. What is the actual behavior?
options: The personal host pool's scaling plan will create and remove session hosts exactly like a pooled host pool
A personal host pool's scaling plan can only start or deallocate its existing, fixed set of dedicated VMs; it cannot create or remove session hosts
Scaling plans cannot be applied to personal host pools at all
The scaling plan will convert the personal host pool into a pooled host pool automatically
questions.explanation: Because every session host in a personal host pool is permanently dedicated to one assigned user, a scaling plan there can only manage the power state (start/deallocate) of the existing VMs; it has no scale-out or scale-in capability to add or remove hosts the way a pooled host pool's autoscale does. Scaling plans are supported on personal host pools, just with this narrower behavior.

questions.question: An administrator wants to inspect the Azure Virtual Desktop Broker and Gateway components directly as resources inside their own Azure subscription, the way they can inspect their session host VMs. What should they expect?
options: These components are visible as read-only resources in the customer's subscription
These components cannot be found because they run in Microsoft's managed control plane, outside the customer's subscription and tenant
They can only be found by searching the customer's Log Analytics workspace resource group
They appear automatically once a scaling plan is created
