questions.explanation: The Broker, Gateway, Web Access, and Diagnostics services are part of the Azure Virtual Desktop control plane, which Microsoft fully manages and hosts outside the customer's own subscription, so they never appear as inspectable resources there. Only the data plane — session hosts, the virtual network, and FSLogix storage — actually lives in and is manageable within the customer's subscription.

questions.question: Users already complete Windows Hello for Business authentication to reach their Azure Virtual Desktop feed, but are then prompted for credentials again the moment they open a session on a session host. What should be configured to eliminate this second prompt?
options: A validation environment flag on the host pool
Single sign-on (SSO) for the host pool using Microsoft Entra Kerberos or certificate-based authentication
FSLogix Application Masking
Depth-first load balancing
questions.explanation: Host pool SSO, using Microsoft Entra Kerberos-based or certificate-based authentication, eliminates the redundant in-session credential prompt for users who already authenticated with a strong method like Windows Hello for Business to reach the feed. The other options address update rings, app visibility, and session distribution, none of which affect the sign-in prompt a user sees when opening a session.

questions.question: An administrator is configuring the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal's permissions so that autoscale scaling plans and Start VM on Connect can power session host VMs on and off, but wants to avoid granting rights to resize or delete those VMs. Which built-in role best fits this least-privilege requirement?
options: Desktop Virtualization Virtual Machine Contributor
Owner
Desktop Virtualization Power On Off Contributor
Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator
questions.explanation: Desktop Virtualization Power On Off Contributor grants only the rights needed to start and stop VMs, which is exactly what autoscale and Start VM on Connect require without exposing broader capabilities like resizing or deleting VMs. Desktop Virtualization Virtual Machine Contributor and Owner both grant far more than power state control alone.

questions.question: A user connects to their Azure Virtual Desktop session and expects their local, client-side printer to appear automatically inside the session without the session host needing that specific printer's vendor driver pre-installed. What makes this possible by default?
options: FSLogix Application Masking
The Remote Desktop Easy Print driver
MSIX app attach
Azure Compute Gallery image versioning
questions.explanation: The Remote Desktop Easy Print driver redirects the client's local printers into the session automatically without requiring that exact printer's vendor driver to be installed on the session host. The other options address application visibility, delivery, and image versioning, none of which relate to printer redirection.

questions.question: A legacy line-of-business application is only available as a traditional Win32 EXE installer with no MSIX package option, and every user of a host pool needs it available. Which delivery approach fits this constraint?
options: MSIX app attach, since it works for any application format
Deploy the Win32 installer to session hosts via Microsoft Intune (or bake it into the golden image)
FSLogix Redirections.xml
Session watermarking
questions.explanation: Since MSIX app attach only works with applications packaged as MSIX, an application only available as a Win32 EXE installer must instead be deployed via Intune Win32 app management or installed directly into the golden image. Redirections.xml and watermarking address profile folder exclusions and screen-content deterrence, not application delivery.

questions.question: An admin needs to trace exactly which stage — client, gateway, broker, or session host — a specific user's failed connection stalled at, using a Kusto query against Log Analytics data. Which tables specifically record each connection's lifecycle events and stage timestamps for this kind of analysis?
options: WVDConnections and WVDCheckpoints
AgentHealthStatus only
CHEAT_SHEET diagnostic logs
The Azure Activity Log
questions.explanation: WVDConnections records each session's connection lifecycle and duration, while WVDCheckpoints records the timestamped stages a connection passed through, together letting an admin pinpoint exactly where a specific connection stalled. The Azure Activity Log records control-plane management operations like resource creation, not per-session connection telemetry.

questions.question: The host pool's max session limit setting controls how many concurrent sessions a single session host will accept before it is considered full.
questions.explanation: That is exactly what the max session limit setting does; it works together with the load-balancing algorithm to decide when a host is full and new sessions should be routed elsewhere or a new host started.

questions.question: Azure Hybrid Benefit provides the same per-core Windows Server licensing discount to Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session session host VM compute as it does to Windows Server workloads.
questions.explanation: Windows 10/11 multi-session VM compute is not eligible for the same per-core Azure Hybrid Benefit discount that Windows Server workloads receive; the realistic cost levers for multi-session host pools are autoscale and Reserved Instances/Savings Plans on the compute instead.

questions.question: A pooled multi-session host pool running on a GPU-enabled VM size still shares that one physical GPU's capacity across every concurrent session running on that host.
questions.explanation: Whether GPU passthrough or GPU partitioning/vGPU is used, all concurrent sessions on a multi-session host draw from the same physical GPU's capacity, so GPU-bound capacity planning matters just as much as vCPU/RAM sizing for graphics-intensive workloads.

questions.question: Session hosts must have a public IP address with an inbound NSG rule allowing RDP from the internet so the Azure Virtual Desktop Gateway can reach them.
questions.explanation: Session hosts initiate an outbound-only connection to the Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure and never need a public IP or an inbound internet-facing RDP rule; the Gateway brokers connections without ever needing to reach the session host on an internet-facing inbound port.

questions.question: Which two of the following are accurate distinctions between Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 Cloud PC? (Choose two.)
options: Windows 365 Cloud PC uses fixed, predictable per-user monthly pricing rather than Azure consumption billing
Azure Virtual Desktop cannot publish RemoteApp programs, only full desktops
Azure Virtual Desktop supports pooled, multi-session host pools that Windows 365 Cloud PCs cannot be part of
Windows 365 Cloud PCs support autoscale scaling plans identical to pooled AVD host pools
questions.explanation: Windows 365 uses fixed per-user monthly pricing instead of Azure consumption billing, and only Azure Virtual Desktop supports pooling multiple users onto shared multi-session hardware, since a Cloud PC is always a fixed, dedicated single-user VM. Azure Virtual Desktop does support RemoteApp, and Windows 365 Cloud PCs have no pooled-host-pool-style autoscale since each Cloud PC is a single dedicated VM.

questions.question: Which two of the following are legitimate ways to make an application available to Azure Virtual Desktop users? (Choose two.)
options: Deploying a Win32 installer to session hosts via Microsoft Intune
Publishing the application through MSIX app attach
Configuring the application in FSLogix Redirections.xml
Enabling drain mode on the session host
questions.explanation: Deploying via Intune Win32 app management and delivering via MSIX app attach are both legitimate, commonly used ways to make an application available to users. Redirections.xml only excludes folders from the FSLogix profile container, and drain mode only controls whether a host accepts new sessions — neither delivers an application.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about monitoring and maintaining the Azure Virtual Desktop agent and connection health? (Choose two.)
options: Scheduled agent updates let an admin define a maintenance window for automatic AVD agent and side-by-side stack updates
The WVDConnections Log Analytics table records each session's connection lifecycle and duration
Scheduled agent updates also control Windows OS update timing, replacing Azure Update Manager entirely
The WVDConnections table only stores data for personal host pools, never pooled host pools
questions.explanation: Scheduled agent updates control when the AVD agent/side-by-side stack is allowed to update, and WVDConnections records each session's connection lifecycle and duration for KQL analysis. Scheduled agent updates have no effect on Windows OS patching, which is still handled by tools like Azure Update Manager, and WVDConnections records data for both pooled and personal host pools.

cheatSheet.heading: Exam-day strategy
points: You have 120 minutes for 50 questions — about 2.4 minutes each on average. Budget more time for multi-part scenario questions and less for straight recall, rather than pacing every question identically.
Real scoring isn't a flat percentage of questions right (some count for more than others) — treat 70%+ as a safe buffer to aim for, not an exact threshold to just clear.

Flag anything you're unsure of and move on rather than stalling — a question later in the exam can sometimes jog a detail you needed earlier, and you get partial credit for nothing by running out of time on one question.
On multi-select ('choose N') questions, eliminate the options you're confident are wrong first; guessing among 2 plausible answers beats guessing among 4.
Your first read of a question is usually right — change an answer only when you find a specific detail you missed, not from general second-guessing.

cheatSheet.heading: Host pool types: personal vs. pooled
points: Personal host pool = 1:1 static user-to-VM assignment (assigned or automatic); user state persists on that same VM between sessions.
Pooled host pool = many users share a pool of session hosts; pair it with FSLogix so a user's profile and settings roam regardless of which host they land on.
Pooled load balancing: Breadth-first spreads new sessions across all available hosts first; Depth-first fills one host to its max session limit before moving to the next.
Validation environment host pools receive AVD service updates first — use them to test changes before rolling out to production pools.
Direct assignment (personal) means manually assigning a user to a specific VM; automatic assignment lets AVD assign the first user who connects.

cheatSheet.heading: FSLogix profile containers
points: Profile Container redirects the entire user profile into a VHD/VHDX on file storage (Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files, typically) so it roams between session hosts.
Office Container isolates just the Outlook/OneDrive cache data — used when you don't want the full profile roamed, or alongside Profile Container for large mailbox caches.
Concurrent multi-user pooled scenarios need storage with enough IOPS — Azure Files Premium or Azure NetApp Files are common choices over a Standard file share.
Only one user session can mount a given VHD(X) at a time — a locked profile from a crashed or disconnected session is the classic 'stuck on temp profile' troubleshooting scenario.
Cloud Cache is FSLogix's option for replicating profile data across multiple storage locations for redundancy or multi-region scenarios.

cheatSheet.heading: Session host sizing & scaling
points: Native autoscale on a host pool can start/stop or scale hosts in/out on a schedule — it superseded the older, separate scaling-plan preview tooling.
Personal host pools can only start/stop existing VMs on autoscale; they cannot scale out new VMs or deallocate-and-remove the way pooled pools can.
Sizing is driven by user profile — light/medium/heavy workers need progressively more vCPU/RAM per user, which lowers users-per-host density as workload gets heavier.
An autoscale schedule has four phases — ramp-up, peak, ramp-down, off-peak — each with its own load-balancing algorithm and capacity thresholds.

cheatSheet.heading: Networking (RDP Shortpath & Multipath)
points: RDP Shortpath opens a direct UDP transport between client and session host, bypassing the TCP-based reverse connect path for lower latency.
Shortpath for managed networks needs a direct/private path (VPN or ExpressRoute) between client and host; Shortpath for public networks works over the open internet.
If a direct path can't be established, AVD automatically falls back to the standard reverse connect transport over TCP 443 — the session still connects, just less optimally.
RDP Multipath/multi-transport is about session resilience — automatically reconnecting after a brief network blip — not raw throughput.

cheatSheet.heading: Identity & security for AVD
points: AVD supports pure Microsoft Entra ID-joined session hosts as well as hybrid Entra-joined (Entra ID + on-prem AD) hosts — pure Entra ID-join removes the need for domain-controller line of sight for many scenarios.
Entra ID-joined session hosts run Windows 10/11 Enterprise multi-session or single-session and support single sign-on so users are not prompted twice.
Conditional Access applies to AVD like any other app — enforce MFA or a compliant-device requirement against the Azure Virtual Desktop cloud app.

RBAC roles like Desktop Virtualization User (assign to end users) and Desktop Virtualization Contributor (assign to admins) control who can use vs. manage a host pool — don't confuse resource-level Azure RBAC with in-session app permissions.

cheatSheet.heading: Monitoring (Azure Monitor for AVD / Insights)
points: Azure Monitor for AVD (AVD Insights) combines host pool health, session host performance counters, and user connection diagnostics in one dashboard.
Diagnostics data lands in a Log Analytics workspace — you must enable and configure Insights, it doesn't capture detailed data by default.
Connection diagnostics trace a specific failed or slow connection through each stage: client, gateway, broker, session host.

cheatSheet.heading: Exam-day reminders
points: AZ-140 is a Specialty-level certification and, like other Microsoft role-based/specialty certs, requires annual renewal via a free online assessment.
'Each user needs their own persistent desktop with locally customized apps' points to a personal host pool; 'many users share stateless desktops' points to pooled + FSLogix.

'Lowest latency over the managed corporate network' points to Shortpath for managed networks; 'connecting over the internet without a VPN' points to Shortpath for public networks or the reverse connect fallback.
Don't confuse MSIX app attach (dynamically attaching a virtualized app at sign-in without installing it on the image) with an app fully installed in the golden image.
